title: CLR/18/2012 of SYEEDA BEGUM Vs BASANT KUMAR and OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
Civil Revision No. 18 of 2012
Syeeda Begum, W/o Islam Khan
R/o Village Salempur Mehdood
Pargana Roorkee, Tehsil and District Haridwar
 ÖÖÖÖÖ.Revisionist/Plaintiff
Versus
1. Basant Kumar, S/o Fateh Chand
2. Ravinder Kumar, S/o Shri Lakhan
3. Sibbu, S/o Shri Lakhan
All R/o Village Bahadarabad
Tehsil and District Haridwar
 ÖÖÖÖÖ. Respondents/Defendants
Mr. Siddhartha Singh, Advocate, present for the revisionist/plaintiff.
Mr. Pankaj Miglani, Advocate, present for the respondents/defendants.
Honíble Prafulla C. Pant,J.
Heard.
2. This revision is directed against the order dated
03.03.2012, passed by Civil Judge (Sr. Div.) Haridwar,
in Suit No. 80 of 2011, whereby said court has
dismissed the application 68A moved by the plaintiff
for withdrawal of the suit with permission to file a
fresh.
3. Sub-Rule (3) of Rule 1 of order 23 of Code of Civil
Procedure, 1908 (for short C.P.C.) provides that where
the court is satisfied that a suit must fail by reason of
some formal defect, or that there are sufficient grounds

2
for allowing the plaintiff to institute a fresh suit for the
subject matter of a suit or part of a claim, it may, on
such terms as it thinks fit, grant the plaintiff permission
to withdraw from such suit or such part of the claim
with liberty to institute a fresh suit.
4. The plaintiff in her application 68A stated before
the trial court that the plaint is not accompanied with
the site plan of the disputed property, nor it could be
pleaded as to how on the basis of the ëWillí Usman Ali
Khan became owner in possession of the disputed
property, nor it is mentioned in the plaint that a part of
the disputed property has already been sold on
24.08.2011 (subsequent to filing of the plaint) as such
the plaintiff be allowed to withdraw the suit with
liberty to file a fresh. The trial court has rejected the
application only on the ground that the plaintiff could
have moved amendment application to remove the
defects.
5. Learned counsel for the revisionist submitted that
after amendment in Rule 17 Order 6 of Code of Civil
Procedure, vide Act No. 22 of 2002 it is not easy to get
the plaint amended as it is used to be before the proviso
added to Rule 17 of Order 6 of the Code. On the other
hand, learned counsel for the defendants submitted

3
that the permission to file suit a fresh is not matter of
right.
6. Having considered submissions of learned counsel
for the rival parties and after going through the
impugned order, in the above circumstances, this Court
is of the view that the trial court has erred in law in
rejecting the application 68A moved by the plaintiff
seeking to withdraw the suit with permission to file a
fresh. It is not a case where the application of the
plaintiff was malafide, nor it is a case where the
plaintiff has desired to file a suit a fresh after he has lost
right to maintain the suit on the cause of action for
which the suit was filed, nor the harassment appears to
have been attempted to be caused to the defendants.
7. Therefore, without prejudice to the rights of the
parties this revision is allowed. Impugned order dated
03.03.2012 passed by Civil Judge (Sr. Div.), Haridwar,
in Suit No. 80 of 2011 is hereby set aside. Application
68A filed by the plaintiff under Order 23 Rule 1(3) of
C.P.C. for withdrawal of the suit with permission to file
a fresh is allowed. Suit no. 80 of 2011 stands withdrawn
with liberty to file a fresh without prejudice to the
rights of the parties.
 (Prafulla C. Pant, J.)
Parul 10.05.2013
